distance.locator: MINOS detector paper, §1 Introduction (overview of the experiment)
distance.note: Target-to-far-detector distance. The Fermilab end is site:fermilab-main-campus, a campus-grade point (precision 3 km), not the target; the Soudan end is the surveyed MINOS far-detector midpoint (site:soudan-minos-far-detector). The great-circle distance between the two recorded points is 735.4 km (0.01 % from the stated value). The same paper gives the surveyed figure as "735.3380 km from the upstream end of the first horn of the neutrino beamline" (§6.5, Far detector location); the NuMI beam paper (NIM A 806) gives 734 km, without a stated reference point (not a rounding of 735.3 km): "encountering the MINOS Far Detector (FD) 734 km away in the Soudan Mine in Minnesota".
distance.quote: The far detector, shown in Fig. 1, is located in Soudan, MN (47.8◦ N latitude, and 92.2◦ W longitude), 735.3 km from the NuMI beam production target at Fermilab

distance.locator: NOvA monopole-search paper (arXiv:2512.20294), §II NOvA Far Detector; PRD 106, 032004, §II
distance.note: Target-to-far-detector distance as the NOvA collaboration quotes it; the 2022 oscillation paper says "The 14 kt Far Detector (FD) is located at Ash River, Minnesota, ~810 km from the source." The Fermilab end is site:fermilab-main-campus, a campus-grade point (precision 3 km); the Ash River end is the NOvA far-detector point, which the collaboration quotes only to 0.1 degree (precision 8 km). The great-circle distance between the two recorded points is 811.7 km (0.2 % from the stated value).
distance.quote: the 14 kt Far Detector (FD) is located on the surface, 810 km from the target, near Ash River, Minnesota

direction.locator: NuMI beam paper section 2.1 (inclination); MINOS detector paper sections 1 (distance) and 6.5 (direction)
direction.note: Distance: the MINOS detector paper says the far detector is "735.3 km from the NuMI beam production target at Fermilab" (section 1; section 6.5 gives the surveyed 735.3380 km "from the upstream end of the first horn of the neutrino beamline"). The NuMI beam paper gives a different figure, "encountering the MINOS Far Detector (FD) 734 km away in the Soudan Mine in Minnesota", without stating its reference point; 735.3 km is used here and in the baseline. Direction: the MINOS paper says the beam "travels approximately NNW" (section 6.5), and the NuMI paper says it continues "further north through the Earth’s crust".
direction.quote: To point towards the Soudan Laboratory the proton beam had to be inclined downward by 58 mrad.
direction.value: north-north-west from Fermilab, inclined 58 mrad (3.34 degrees) downward towards the Soudan mine in Minnesota, 735.3 km from the NuMI target

intervals.label: MINOS-era operation
intervals.quote: Its focus is the beam configuration in place during the data taking of the MINOS experiment, from May 20, 2005 until April 30, 2012.

intervals.label: accelerator shutdown
intervals.note: Long accelerator shutdown between the end of MINOS data taking and the NuMI restart.
intervals.quote: After a long accelerator shutdown following the completion of the MINOS experiment, the NuMI beam was restarted in September 2013

intervals.label: NOvA / MINOS+ / MINERvA era
intervals.locator: end: Fermilab PAC report, April 2026 meeting, findings on accelerator status
intervals.note: End = July 2024, when the Main Injector last operated: "The MI has not operated since July 2024" (Fermilab PAC, April 2026 meeting); "Following the record achievement [1.018 MW to NuMI, June 2024], the Main Injector complex suffered a series of failures that have prevented NuMI beam." (IPAC'26).
intervals.quote: the NuMI beam was restarted in September 2013 for two new experiments

intervals.label: last reported: no NuMI beam
intervals.locator: Fermilab PAC report April 2026; PAC NuMI mini-meeting report July 2025 ("There was no beam delivery for MI since 2024")
intervals.note: Last reported beam condition; restart is not confirmed in the Atlas source audit on 2026-11-19. The open end retains the last reported condition as an assumption, not a new observation that the shutdown persisted. The April 2026 PAC report says MI had not operated since July 2024; the Fall 2026 report (PDF pages 4-5) still describes stable beam on 1 October as planned and the restart as upcoming. The proposed NuMI run remains a separate planned interval. A later report of operation should close this interval; passing a scheduled date must not do so.
intervals.quote: Following the record achievement, the Main Injector complex suffered a series of failures that have prevented NuMI beam.

intervals.label: NuMI run (planned: 12 weeks, stretch goal 20)
intervals.locator: Fall 2026 PAC report, PDF page 4, accelerator-complex findings (FY27 run and planned stable beam); April 2026 report, PDF page 3, stretch schedule
intervals.note: A schedule, not a reported event. The Fall 2026 PAC report plans 12 weeks of FY27 operation, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks; stable MI beam was planned for 1 October 2026. The February 2027 end retains the April report stretch schedule. The source audit on 2026-11-19 found no later confirmation of this run in the reviewed primary sources.
intervals.quote: The plan is for 12 weeks of operation in FY27, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks of operation, with a focus on the NuMI beam.

name: NuMI (Neutrinos at the Main Injector) beamline
notes: Near-detector baselines are not recorded: the MINOS, MINERvA and NOvA near detectors all sit on site:fermilab-main-campus, the same campus point as the beamline, so no site-to-site distance exists. Sourced figures for when separate near-detector sites exist: the MINOS near detector is "1040 m from the primary target" (MINOS detector paper, §6.1); the NOvA near detector is "located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target" (arXiv:2512.20294).

primary_beam.quote: steering a 120 GeV proton beam onto a narrow graphite target

energy.quote: The NuMI beam facility produces neutrinos by steering a 120 GeV proton beam onto a narrow graphite target approximately 1 m in length through a collimating baffle.

secondary_beam.quote: the produced hadrons are focused by two magnetic horns and then enter a 675 m long decay volume
secondary_beam.value: muon neutrinos / antineutrinos from a 675 m decay volume; on-axis for MINOS/MINOS+/MINERvA, 14.6 mrad off-axis for NOvA

beam_power.note: Original design beam power; the NOvA-era design goal quoted in the same paper is 700 kW.
beam_power.quote: The design beam power was somewhat optimistically set to 400 kW

off_axis_angle.note: Off-axis angle of the NOvA near and far detectors relative to the NuMI beam axis; MINOS, MINOS+ and MINERvA sit on axis.
off_axis_angle.quote: The two detectors are placed 14.6 mrad off-axis from the center of the neutrino beam

proton_energy.quote: the 120 GeV protons extracted from the Fermilab Main Injector

summary.plain: Fermilab’s long-running neutrino beam. Protons hit a graphite target and the particles that come out decay into neutrinos aimed at detectors in Minnesota.
summary.technical: 120 GeV Main Injector protons on a 1 m graphite target, two magnetic horns and a 675 m decay volume, aimed 58 mrad downward toward Soudan. Served MINOS (2005-2012) and, since September 2013, NOvA (14.6 mrad off axis), MINOS+ and MINERvA.

target.quote: a narrow graphite target approximately 1 m in length through a collimating baffle
target.value: graphite target approximately 1 m in length
